title: Module 8: Administration & Monitoring
content: Ensuring health, performance, and visibility in AMPS 🛠️
Overview of the AMPS monitoring ecosystem
speakerNotes: Welcome to Module 8. Today we focus on how to keep your AMPS instance running smoothly and how to peek inside the engine using the built-in monitoring tools.

title: Why Monitoring Matters
speakerNotes: Without monitoring, you're flying blind. AMPS is designed for low latency, so even small deviations in performance can be critical.

title: The AMPS Monitoring Stack
content: AMPS provides multiple ways to consume health data:
mermaid:
graph TD
    A[AMPS Engine] --> B[Stats Database (stats.db)]
    B --> C[REST API (/amps)]
    C --> D[Galvanometer (Web UI)]
    A --> E[Event Logs (Files/Syslog)]
    A --> F[Internal Topics (/AMPS/.*)]
speakerNotes: The statistics flow from the engine to a SQLite database, which is exposed via REST, and finally visualized in the Galvanometer.

title: The Galvanometer (Web UI)
content: No separate installation required (bundled with server)
Real-time visibility into CPU, memory, and message rates
speakerNotes: The Galvanometer is your first stop for a quick health check. It's a JavaScript app served directly by AMPS.

title: Galvanometer Features
content: **Topic Browser**: Query/Subscribe to any topic directly 🔍
**Grid Display**: Inspect SOW records in real-time
speakerNotes: One of the most powerful features is the Topic Browser. It allows you to verify data flow without writing a single line of client code.

title: RESTful Statistics Interface
speakerNotes: If you want to integrate AMPS with external tools like Prometheus or Grafana, the REST API is the way to do it.

title: Time Range Queries
content: Access historical data using `t0` and `t1` parameters:
speakerNotes: You can pull historical trends directly from the REST API. All timestamps must be in UTC ISO-8601 format.

title: Statistics Database (stats.db)
content: Allows deep analysis using standard SQL tools
speakerNotes: By default, stats are in memory. For production, ALWAYS persist them to a file so you can analyze crashes or performance spikes after a restart.

title: Configuring Administration
speakerNotes: The SQLTransport element is crucial—it tells the Galvanometer which transport to use for its built-in query tools.

title: Event Logging Overview
speakerNotes: Logging is your trail of breadcrumbs. Every message has a unique ID, making it easy to search for specific events.

title: Log Levels & Filtering
speakerNotes: Be careful with 'trace' in production—it logs every single message and can fill up your disks very quickly.

title: Log Rotation & Formatting
speakerNotes: Log rotation prevents a single file from consuming all disk space. The '%n' mask is useful for creating a sequence of numbered log files.

title: Monitoring Topics (/AMPS/ClientStatus)
content: Internal event stream for client activity 🔔
Allows applications to react to peer status changes
speakerNotes: The ClientStatus topic is essentially 'AMPS meta-messaging'. You can write apps that alert you whenever a critical publisher disconnects.

title: Monitoring Topics (/AMPS/SOWStats)
speakerNotes: SOWStats is great for monitoring the 'fullness' of your cache. If record counts spike unexpectedly, you might have a logic error in your publishers.

title: Module Summary
content: Use **Galvanometer** for daily checks and ad-hoc queries 🛠️
Use **REST API** for automation and tool integration 🤖
Subscribe to **/AMPS/** topics for real-time reactive monitoring 📡
speakerNotes: That concludes Module 8. You now have the tools to ensure your AMPS deployment remains healthy and observable.
